title: The Witness of Bellwether Lane
premise: Lior Thornbury, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made them the unofficial archivist of Bellwether Lane's secrets, is hired by a nervous stranger who pays triple to prove a murder hasn't happened yet — the murder of councilman Aldous Vane, dated three days out in a ledger Lior once catalogued and dismissed as fiction. As Lior traces the ledger's cipher through town records, they discover it was written by their own missing mentor, and that half of Bellwether Lane's respected families are implicated in a decades-old land fraud Vane was about to expose. In the climax, Lior decodes the final entry in the burning archive house and realizes the 'client' who hired them is the intended victim staging his own death to flush out his enemies; Lior must choose between exposing everyone, including themselves as an unwitting accomplice, or letting the town keep its comfortable lies. They choose truth — narrowly surviving, publishing the ledger, and finally belonging to Bellwether Lane on honest terms rather than as its keeper of secrets.
about_author: Bram Nystrom is a former municipal records clerk from the northern coast who spent eleven years filing other people's paperwork before turning to crime fiction. He writes in longhand at a harbor café and claims every small town he's lived in has taught him something about the weight of silence.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A hooded client leaves an envelope of cash and a photograph of councilman Aldous Vane with one instruction: prove the murder on the enclosed ledger page hasn't happened yet. Lior recognizes the page's cipher style from files catalogued years ago under their vanished mentor's name. The beat is uneasy curiosity curdling into dread as Lior realizes the payment is hush-shaped, not help-shaped.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, intercut with Vane's journal entries. Following the cipher through property deeds and church donation books, Lior maps a land-fraud network binding the lane's oldest families — including the police chief who warns them off with unsettling warmth. The emotional beat is the loneliness of seeing clearly: every friendly face now reads like a filed document, and Lior's gift becomes a burden.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The mentor's trail leads to the condemned archive house, where Lior decodes the final entry hours before hired hands torch it: the ledger names its own author's disappearance as murder, and predicts Vane's death as retaliation for exposure. Escaping the fire with scorched pages, Lior confronts the client — revealed to be Vane himself, faking his death to smoke out his killers. The beat is betrayal and vertigo; Lior was never the detective, only the bait.

chapters.title: Bellwether, Ringing
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. With Vane hidden and the town hunting a corpse that won't die, Lior publishes the decoded ledger at the founders' day assembly, naming names — including their own complicity in filing the evidence away three years ago. The chief is arrested, the families scatter or confess, and Vane walks out alive into disgrace. The resolution lands on belonging earned through truth: Bellwether Lane finally knows Lior, and Lior no longer needs to be its memory.
